name: TJA1145TKJ
title: High-speed CAN transceiver with partial networking and SPI
summary: A high-speed CAN transceiver for automotive nodes that stay on the battery and sleep when idle. It wakes on a standard CAN wake-up pattern, on an ISO 11898-6 selective wake-up frame matched against stored ID, mask and data registers, or on an edge at WAKE, and its INH output switches the node's regulators off in Sleep. An SPI port (16, 24 or 32 bits) sets modes and reads status and events; VIO sets the logic levels for 3.3 V to 5 V controllers. The /FD types stay asleep through CAN FD traffic, never treating an FD frame as a wake-up. SO14 or HVSON14.
key_figures: IBAT 40 µA typ, 59 µA max (-40 °C to 85 °C, VBAT 7 V to 18 V)
VBAT 4.5 V to 28 V; VCC 4.5 V to 5.5 V; VIO 2.85 V to 5.5 V

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A battery-powered CAN node. BAT passes a series diode onto a protected rail that carries a 22 µF electrolytic, the TJA1145 BAT pin and the inputs of a 5 V and a 3 V regulator. INH drives the enable inputs of both regulators, so Sleep mode switches the node's supplies off. The 5 V output feeds VCC; the 3 V output feeds VIO and the microcontroller supply. A resistor from the protected rail pulls up a switch to ground; that node has 10 nF to ground and reaches WAKE through 10 kΩ. SCSN, SDO, SCK and SDI go to ordinary microcontroller port pins; RXD and TXD go to the microcontroller's RXD and TXD pins. CANH and CANL each carry an RT to a centre node with 4.7 nF to ground (split termination).

operation.text: Five operating modes, run by a system controller: Off, Standby, Normal, Sleep and Overtemp. MC in register 01h selects Normal (111), Standby (100) or Sleep (001).
Everything is available; the CAN transceiver mode is then chosen with CMC. Normal is entered from Standby or Sleep by SPI.

Low-current mode: the transceiver cannot send or receive, but INH stays at VBAT so regulators it controls stay on. With CWE = 1 the receiver watches the bus for a wake-up; the bus lines sit at GND through Ri(cm) while idle and near 2.5 V while the bus is active. A standard wake-up pattern wakes the part, or a selective wake-up frame when CPNC = PNCOK = 1. RXD goes LOW on any enabled wake-up or interrupt. Standby is entered from Off once VBAT passes Vth(det)pon, from Overtemp once the chip cools below Tth(rel)otp, from Sleep on a wake-up or interrupt, by SPI (MC = 100), or from Normal when Sleep is requested with a wake-up pending or with every wake-up source disabled.

As Standby, but INH goes high-ohmic so regulators it enables turn off and BAT current falls to its minimum. Sleep ends on any wake-up or interrupt that is enabled, or on SPI access while VIO is supplied. A Sleep request (MC = 001) is obeyed only when no wake-up is pending and CAN or WAKE wake-up (a regular source) is enabled; otherwise the part goes to Standby and, with SPIFE = 1, pulls RXD LOW.

operation.topic: Forced Sleep on VCC or VIO undervoltage
operation.text: If VCC or VIO stays below its undervoltage threshold for longer than the detection delay, the part is forced into Sleep. Captured events (61h to 64h) are cleared, CAN wake-up (CWE = 1) and both WAKE edges (WPFE = WPRE = 1) are enabled, selective wake-up is disabled (CPNC = 0) and PNCOK is cleared, so the node can always wake. FSMS = 1 records the forced entry, so software can restore its wake-up settings after waking.

Off is the state at first battery connection and whenever VBAT falls below Vth(det)poff; CAN pins and INH are high-ohmic. When VBAT rises above Vth(det)pon the part initialises and enters Standby after tstartup.

From Normal the part enters Overtemp at once when the chip passes Tth(act)otp: transmitter and receiver are off and the CAN pins high-ohmic. No new wake-up is detected, though a pending one still holds RXD LOW. It returns to Standby below Tth(rel)otp, or goes to Off if VBAT falls below Vth(det)poff. Above Tth(warn)otp the part sets OTWS and, with OTWE = 1, raises the OTW interrupt.

High-speed CAN to ISO 11898-2, -5 and -6, up to 1 Mbit/s. VCC supplies the transmitter and BAT the receiver. CANH and CANL are biased to 2.5 V in Active and Listen-only modes. In Offline mode the bias is autonomous, drawn from VBAT: 2.5 V while the bus is active (Offline Bias) and GND after tto(silence) without activity (Offline).

The transceiver drives and receives the bus when MC = 111, CMC = 01 or 10, and VCC is above Vuvd(VCC). In this mode VCC supplies the bias; a VCC drop under Vuvd(VCC) sends the transceiver to Offline with autonomous bias. If TXD is LOW when Active is selected, the transceiver stays in Listen-only until TXD goes HIGH. With CMC = 10 a VCC undervoltage does not end Active mode at once; the transmitter stays on until the forced Sleep. CTS shows whether the transmitter is ready.

Selected by CMC = 11 in Normal mode: the receiver and bias stay on and the transmitter is off, so the node hears the bus without affecting it. The transceiver also stays in Listen-only when Active is selected while VCC is below 90 % of nominal.

operation.topic: CAN Offline and Offline Bias modes
operation.text: Offline watches for a CAN wake-up (with CWE = 1) with the bus biased to GND. Bus activity switches it to Offline Bias, with the bus at 2.5 V, and silence for longer than tto(silence) returns it to Offline. Offline Bias applies in Standby or Sleep, in Normal with CMC = 00, in Normal with CMC = 01 and VCC below 90 %, and after a bus wake-up. Offline applies after those conditions last longer than tto(silence), and on leaving Off or Overtemp.

The transceiver is fully off with floating bus lines in Off and Overtemp modes, and when VBAT is below Vuvd(CAN). It returns via Offline once VBAT exceeds Vuvr(CAN) and the part has left Off/Overtemp.

With the transceiver Offline, CWE = 1, and selective wake-up off (CPNC = 0 or PNCOK = 0), a dominant, recessive, dominant sequence wakes the part: each dominant phase at least twake(busdom), the recessive phase at least twake(busrec), all within tto(wake). Extra pulses between the phases are allowed. A wake-up sets CW and pulls RXD LOW; from Sleep it also switches INH to VBAT and enters Standby.

With CWE = 1, CPNC = 1 and PNCOK = 1 only a matching wake-up frame (ISO 11898-1 frame: ID, DLC, data, CRC with delimiter) wakes the part. IDE picks 11-bit or 29-bit IDs; the ID registers hold the identifier and the mask registers mark don't-care bits. With PNDM = 0 a match needs only the masked ID and an error-free CRC. With PNDM = 1 (default) the frame must also not be a remote frame, its DLC must equal the stored DLC, and for DLC > 0 at least one data bit set to 1 must line up with a 1 in the data masks; each such pair is one group of nodes, up to 64 groups. With DLC = 0 the data masks are ignored; with DLC above 0 and all data mask bits 0 the bus cannot wake the part (data masks reset to all 1s). A DLC mismatch wakes nothing. CDR selects the CAN data rate used for selective wake-up, 50 kbit/s to 1000 kbit/s.

Frames with errors ahead of the ACK field count up an internal counter; error-free frames count it down. Bus data between the CRC delimiter and the next SOF is ignored. Past 31 the counter sets PNFDE and the part wakes; it resets when the bias switches off and partial networking is enabled again. Writing any partial networking configuration register clears PNCOK, which software sets again after configuring.

With CFDC = 1 the /FD types count a received CAN FD control field down on the error counter and then ignore the bus until idle, so they stay asleep with partial networking on while CAN FD traffic runs. CAN FD frames never count as wake-up frames, even with PNDM = 0 and a matching ID. In TJA1145T, TJA1145TK, and in /FD types with CFDC = 0, CAN FD frames count as errors, and enough of them overflow the counter and wake the part.

In Active mode a LOW on TXD lasting longer than tto(dom)TXD turns the transmitter off and frees the bus to recessive; TXD going HIGH resets the timer. This sets a lowest bit rate of 15 kbit/s. The event sets CFS, clears CTS and, with CFE = 1, raises CF.

operation.topic: VCC undervoltage and loss of BAT
operation.text: With CMC = 01, VCC falling below Vuvd(VCC) sets VCS and raises CF if enabled. Losing the BAT supply does not load the bus or the microcontroller, and no reverse current flows from the bus.
WPRE enables wake-up on a rising edge at WAKE and WPFE on a falling edge. When local wake-up is not used it should be disabled and WAKE tied to GND for best EMI behaviour. WPVS reads the WAKE level.

operation.topic: Wake-up and interrupt events on RXD
operation.text: Regular wake-up events are CW, WPR and WPF; interrupt events are PO, OTW, SPIF, PNFDE, CBS and CF. PO and PNFDE are always captured, the rest only when enabled in 04h, 23h and 4Ch. A captured event sets its status bit; in CAN Offline mode RXD goes LOW; in Sleep, INH goes HIGH and the part enters Standby. The global status register 60h shows which group (system, transceiver, WAKE) holds an event. A status bit is cleared by writing 1 to it; clearing only the bits seen set in the last read avoids losing events that arrive just before the write.

Clearing an event bit releases RXD HIGH and starts a td(event) timer. Events during the timer are recorded; if any are pending when it expires RXD goes LOW again, so several events cost one interrupt.
Sleep is entered only when a regular wake-up source (CAN or WAKE) is on and every event status bit is clear; otherwise a Sleep command (MC = 001) leads to Standby.
Register 7Eh identifies the part: 70h for TJA1145T/TK and 74h for the /FD types. Register 0Ah write-protects address areas against SPI writes. Four bytes of general-purpose RAM sit at 06h to 09h.
VIO connects to the microcontroller supply; TXD, RXD and the SPI pins then work at the microcontroller's levels without level shifters, from 3.3 V to 5 V.

Full-duplex SPI, multi-slave capable: SCSN active LOW, SCK idle LOW (pull-down), SDI in, SDO high-impedance with SCSN HIGH. Data are sampled on the falling SCK edge and shifted on the rising edge, MSB first. The first byte is a 7-bit address followed by a read-only bit (1 = read, SDI data ignored); then one, two or three data bytes follow, giving 16-, 24- or 32-bit frames with the address incrementing per byte. The addressed register contents come back on SDO. A write with a bit count other than 16, 24 or 32 is dropped and sets SPIF. Writes to absent registers are tolerated; writes past 7Fh wrap to 00h. A read longer than 32 bits echoes SDI onto SDO from bit 33. The register space is 128 bytes, 00h to 7Fh. An SPI access under way during an automatic mode change is ignored.

Split termination: at bus end nodes RT = 60 Ω each from CANH and CANL to a centre point with a capacitor (for example 4.7 nF) to ground; sub-nodes may use a weak termination such as RT = 1.3 kΩ if the OEM requires it.
Qualified to AEC-Q100 for automotive use. ESD: 8 kV HBM on the bus pins; 6 kV IEC 61000-4-2 on BAT, WAKE and the bus pins. Bus pins withstand shorts to 58 V. Suitable for 12 V and 24 V systems.
Both packages are reflow-solderable; peak temperature by package thickness and volume follows J-STD-020D. The moisture sensitivity level marked on the packing applies.
